title: Linear-size circuits for stable ternary compaction
formal: Is there a universal constant \(C\ge1\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\), stable ternary compaction \(S_n:\{0,1,2\}^n\to\{0,1,2\}^n\) is computable by a Boolean circuit with at most \(Cn\) gates? The function deletes all symbols \(2\), retains all symbols \(0,1\) in their original relative order, and appends the deleted number of \(2\)s on the right. Circuits use the binary alphabet encoding and bounded-fan-in basis specified below, with no depth or uniformity restriction.
definitions: Encode symbols \(0,1,2\) by \(00,01,10\), respectively, using a fixed ordered pair of bits for each input position. A circuit for length \(n\) is a finite acyclic directed Boolean circuit with \(2n\) ordered input bits and \(2n\) ordered output bits. Its non-input gates are binary AND, binary OR, unary NOT and optional constant-0 or constant-1 gates. Each such gate, including a constant gate, contributes one to size. Fan-out is unrestricted. Wires and output designations have no separate cost, and the same gate or input can feed multiple gates and outputs. The circuit is deterministic. It must be correct on every concatenation of valid input encodings; behavior on any input containing a pair \(11\) is unrestricted. For \(a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in\{0,1,2\}^n\), let \(i_1<\cdots<i_m\) be exactly the indices where \(a_i\ne2\). The required output encodes \(a_{i_1}\cdots a_{i_m}\) followed by \(n-m\) copies of \(2\). This definition includes \(m=0\) and \(m=n\). In particular, it preserves the relative order of a \(0\) and a \(1\); it does not sort them against each other. All output positions must be produced by one circuit and their gates are counted jointly. Let \(s(n)\) be the minimum permitted circuit size for this promise function. The quantifiers are \(\exists C\ge1\;\forall n\ge1\;\exists\mathcal C_n\), with \(|\mathcal C_n|\le Cn\) and exact correctness on all valid inputs. The circuit may depend arbitrarily on \(n\), and no algorithm constructing \(\mathcal C_n\) is required. The circuit may compute on the individual encoding bits; it is not restricted to comparing or routing indivisible records.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof that \(s(n)\le Cn\) for some universal \(C\) and all \(n\ge1\), or a complete Lean-checked proof of its negation \(\forall C\ge1\;\exists n\ge1,\ s(n)>Cn\). The negative statement rules out every nonuniform family in the defined unrestricted Boolean model; a lower bound for comparators or indivisible-record routing does not suffice. A conditional result under an additional conjecture settles only that conditional version. A positive answer must retain the original order of the \(0\)s and \(1\)s, with an exact linear size bound rather than a bound multiplied by an unbounded iterated-logarithm factor.
why: This is an elementary deterministic rearrangement whose output preserves an arbitrary binary subsequence. Its sequential simplicity contrasts with the difficulty of arranging all output bits in a fixed circuit. Resolving linear circuit size would sharpen the boundary between data movement with input-dependent access and unrestricted bounded-fan-in Boolean computation.

importance.reason: A specific circuit-size barrier beyond generic lower-bound statements; stable compaction connects elementary data movement with unrestricted Boolean computation.

progress.text: Regan poses the linear-size circuit question for the exact stable ternary function.

The checked v2 of Asharov–Lin–Shi distinguishes its non-stable compaction construction from stable compaction and separates unrestricted Boolean gates from the indivisibility restriction. The work appeared at SODA 2021 and subsequently in SIAM Journal on Computing in 2022.
Lin and Shi’s SODA 2022 paper improves short-key sorting depth; the checked November 2021 manuscript’s Theorem 1.1 and accompanying discussion do not promise stability.

context_blocks.text: Regan’s July 2007 problem defines precisely the order-preserving movement of all dummy symbols to the right. The present two-bit encoding and complete Boolean basis make its nonuniform linear-size target explicit.

Ordinary ternary sorting discards the order between retained zeros and ones. Stable compaction must preserve that binary sequence, so a circuit that only counts occurrences of the three symbols computes a different function.

Asharov, Lin and Shi obtain improved Boolean circuits for compaction and sorting short keys, but their construction deliberately does not preserve stability. Their discussion distinguishes unrestricted Boolean computation from the indivisible-payload model used in some stable-compaction lower bounds.

Lin and Shi’s SODA 2022 work improves the depth of short-key sorting circuits while retaining near-linear size bounds with iterated-logarithm factors in the relevant short-key regime. Its Introduction explicitly states that the sorting is not stable. This result therefore does not provide a linear-size circuit for the stable ternary function.

The checked literature also discusses conditional lower bounds based on the Li–Li network-coding conjecture. Such conditional bounds and lower bounds for restricted data-movement models are not unconditional impossibility results for this card.

sentences: Stable ternary compaction moves every 2 to the end while preserving the order of all zeros and ones.
The question asks whether each input length admits an exact Boolean circuit of size proportional to that length.
Circuits may have arbitrary depth and fan-out and may compute freely on the fixed two-bit alphabet encoding.
Non-stable compaction and ordinary ternary sorting do not retain the binary sequence required in the answer.
The checked short-key sorting advances and conditional or restricted lower bounds do not resolve this nonuniform linear-size question.

status_note: The original author question is from 2007. The checked 2021/2022 sorting advances are non-stable and do not settle its exact linear-size target. Bounded later-work searches through 2026-09-16 found no unconditional resolution in the stated Boolean model; this is a limited review, not a certification of all subsequent literature.
